rejected.title: Managing tourism at Uluru-Kata Tjuta
card: Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park is jointly managed by Anangu Traditional Owners and Parks Australia. A board with an Anangu majority makes the main decisions.
Uluru is sacred to Anangu, and the climb follows a route of great cultural meaning. For many years Anangu asked visitors not to climb.
In 2017 the board decided to close the climb. It closed in October 2019, out of respect for Uluru's cultural meaning.
Other rules guide visitors too, such as not photographing or filming some sacred sites. Visitors can still walk around the base and learn about Anangu culture at the Cultural Centre.
rejected.remember: Joint management lets Anangu law and culture shape how tourists use the park.

a.q: Which best explains why the climb at Uluru closed in 2019?
opts: Respect for Uluru's cultural meaning to Anangu
Too few tourists were visiting the park each year
Parks Australia took control of the park from Anangu
A ban on climbing in all Australian national parks
a.why: Uluru is sacred to Anangu, and the board, which has an Anangu majority, closed the climb out of respect for its cultural meaning. The park is still jointly managed, so Parks Australia did not take control.
a.clue: Think about what Uluru means to Anangu.

b.q: A film crew wants to shoot an advertisement at Uluru, including close-ups of a sacred site. Under the park's management, what is most likely?
opts: It would be asked not to film that site
It could film any site, as the park is public
Parks Australia alone would decide, with no input
The climb would reopen so it could film the top
b.why: Park rules ask visitors not to photograph or film some sacred sites, out of respect for Anangu law. A public park still has rules, and decisions are made jointly, so Parks Australia would not decide alone.
b.clue: Think about the rules for sacred sites.

version.title: Managing tourism at Uluru-Kata Tjuta
card: Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park is jointly managed by Anangu Traditional Owners and Parks Australia. A board with an Anangu majority makes the main decisions.
Uluru is sacred to Anangu, and the climb route has deep cultural meaning. For many years Anangu asked visitors not to climb.
In 2017 the board decided to close the climb. It closed in October 2019, out of respect for Uluru's cultural meaning.
The park still welcomes tourists. They can walk around the base, join a ranger-guided walk and learn about Anangu culture at the Cultural Centre, but some sacred sites must not be photographed.
version.remember: Anangu share in decisions on the park, so their culture shapes how tourists visit Uluru.

a.q: Who decided to close the climb on Uluru?
opts: A park board with an Anangu majority
Parks Australia, without asking Anangu
Tour companies that ran climbs each day
A vote of all the tourists who visited
a.why: The park is jointly managed, and its board, which has an Anangu majority, decided in 2017 to close the climb. Parks Australia shares decisions with Anangu, so it did not decide alone.
a.clue: Think about how the park is managed.

b.q: A school group visits Uluru-Kata Tjuta in 2025. The students want to see Uluru up close and learn about Anangu culture. Which plan fits how the park is managed?
opts: Walk the base, then visit the Cultural Centre
Climb to the top early, before rangers arrive
Photograph every sacred site along the base
Skip the Cultural Centre, as it closed in 2019
b.why: Visitors can still walk around the base and learn about Anangu culture at the Cultural Centre. Climbing is tempting for a close view, but the climb closed in 2019 out of respect for Uluru's cultural meaning.
b.clue: What can visitors still do since 2019?

a.best: A park board with an Anangu majority

b.best: Walk the base, then visit the Cultural Centre
